pr_title: dualstack: use correct IPFamily list for conntrack checks in e2e
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Christopher M. Luciano <cmluciano@us.ibm.com>

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug
/kind failing-test

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
We hardcode the index number in the KubeProxy/Conntrack e2es and
CollectAddresses returns 4 mixed IP Family addresses in a dualstack
cluster. This change ensures that the serverNodeInfo.nodeIP has only
valid addresses for the expected IPFamily per test case.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes: #96024

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

I' ve added logging to conntrack with level v4 recently https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95694 just for these problems, try to bump your kube-proxy logging to v4

@cmluciano seems that there are less  test failures on the IPv6 jobs, let's keep watching them :eyes: 

However, the dual-stack jobs are legit failures, basically because on dualstack clusters, the node has 2 internal IPs, and those tests use the internal IP for asserting some operations, and the problem is that they are picking the internalIP of the wrong IP family, hence the test fails

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b2e1165da8decee2f36a11e98d3dbccbebf82c55/test/e2e/network/conntrack.go#L106

The solution should be to add the InernalIp correspoding to the cluster primary IP familty, you can obtain it with 
```
if framework.TestContext.ClusterIsIPv6()
```

but it seems that we have to modify the `ips := e2enode.CollectAddresses(nodes, v1.NodeInternalIP)` function or add a new one that returns the nodes and the corresponding ips

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b2e1165da8decee2f36a11e98d3dbccbebf82c55/test/e2e/network/kube_proxy.go#L63-L81
Hey @aojea Thanks for all the help, will look into the areas of the code and try to bump the logging.

review_comments: Is that necessary since we are doing a separate hardcoded check of GetAddresses? It works locally on a dualstack cluster.

you don't control the order of the internalIP returned, and if the main family is IPv4 and the ip returned is IPv6 it will fail , actually is the reason why the tests fail today, it connects to an IPv4 service (by default services are SingleStack on the main family) but uses the IPv6 node address to connect to it ...

```

Tue Nov  3 15:13:49 UTC 2020 Try: 1
```
Ah ok, I thought it was just failing bc we also picked the 2nd entry which consistently ended up being the IPv6 address, but that makes sense now.

```

                ips = e2enode.GetAddresses(nodes.Items[1], v1.NodeInternalIP)
